name: Georgia
permitAge: 15 (Class CP instructional permit), after vision and knowledge exams; parent or guardian signs; proof of school enrollment under 18

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including 6 at night (Joshua's Law, DDS); parent or guardian signs a sworn statement, no logbook
teen.holdPermit: 1 year and 1 day before the Class D road test at 16 (georgia.gov)
teen.nightLimit: Class D: no driving late at night; sources disagree on the hours (midnight to 5 a.m. vs midnight to 6 a.m., O.C.G.A. 40-5-24) and on exceptions. Not used in questions.
teen.passengerLimit: Class D (secondary sources): first 6 months only immediate family; second 6 months no more than one non-family passenger under 21; after 12 months no more than three non-family passengers under 21
teen.phone: All drivers: hands-free law since July 1, 2018 (HB 673); no holding or supporting a phone with the body. Mounted GPS allowed.

notes: Learner's permit supervisor: at least 21, licensed for the vehicle, able to take control, in the seat next to the driver (georgia.gov).

Joshua's Law (16 and 17-year-olds since July 1, 2021 for 17): 30-hour approved driver education course plus 6 hours with a certified instructor or the DDS Parent/Teen Driving Guide; 40 supervised hours, 6 at night.
Knowledge test format not confirmed on an official page: secondary sites say 40 questions with 30 correct (75 percent); one says two sections of 20 with 15 correct in each. Left null.
School bus (O.C.G.A. 40-6-163): vehicles in either direction must stop; only on a divided highway may opposite-direction traffic proceed, with caution.

Move Over Law (O.C.G.A. 40-6-16): move over one lane when possible, otherwise slow below the posted limit and be prepared to stop (Governor's Office of Highway Safety). One secondary source mentions a change effective July 1, 2026; not confirmed.
Spanish driver's manual: secondary sources say DDS publishes one; official URL not confirmed. Test-language availability not confirmed.
Under-21 BAC 0.02 from secondary legal sources (O.C.G.A. 40-6-391(k)); not confirmed on an official page.
